explanation: High-fidelity models accurately reflect relevant real-world relationships and constraints. If split deliveries can occur but the model leaves that out, the model is not faithful to the business context. The other choices describe physical design or other database topics, not model fidelity.

options.text: High fidelity, because the model does not reflect an important real-world relationship.
Well-formedness, because every model must always have physical table names.
Normalization, because split deliveries require more foreign keys.
Index design, because route splits affect query speed first.

prompt: A logistics company models deliveries but forgets to represent that some deliveries can be split across multiple routes. Which quality goal is most clearly being missed?
